bihar_raw_news.content: Jan Dhan Yojana: Every fourth account inoperative, Uttar Pradesh tops list; nearly 6 crore have zero balance PM Jan Dhan Yojana: Every fourth account under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is inoperative, while nearly 5.72 crore accounts had zero balance, according to the Finance Ministry's response to activist Chandra Shekhar Gaur's RTI application. Jocelyn Fernandes Updated 6 Sep 2026, 08:30 PM IST Every fourth Jan Dhan account is inoperative, while nearly 5.72 crore accounts had zero balance, according to an RTI reply by the Finance Ministry. ( AI generated image for representational purposes only ) AI Quick Read Jan Dhan Yojana: Every fourth account under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is inoperative, while nearly 5.72 crore accounts had zero balance, as per data given by the Finance Ministry in an RTI reply, PTI reported. Launched as part of the National Mission for Financial Inclusion in August 2014, the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana aims to ensure comprehensive financial inclusion of all households in the country. It provides universal access to banking facilities with at least one basic bank account for every household, financial literacy, and social security cover. Over 59 crore combined balance in Jan Dhan accounts The Finance Ministry's Department of Financial Services ( DFS ) in its response to a Right to Information application by activist Chandra Shekhar Gaur said: Also Read | Central Secretariat Service (CSS) Forum hopes 8th CPC improves CGEIS cover Over 59 crore (59,03,74,907) Jan Dhan accounts hold a combined balance of more than ₹ 3.15 lakh crore ( ₹ 3,15,179.90 crore), as of 12 August 2026, as per the report. Among states, Uttar Pradesh had the highest overall number of accounts at 10.51 crore, followed by Bihar with 7.01 crore accounts, West Bengal with 5.73 crore accounts, Rajasthan with 3.87 crore and Maharashtra with 3.85 crore accounts. The state-wise data was supplied as part of the RTI response and covered 36 Indian states and Union Territories (UTs). In terms of demographics, the RTI reply dated 1 September added that of the total accounts, 32.89 crore were held by women, including transgender account holders, and 26.14 crore were held by men. Uttar Pradesh also had the highest number of zero-balance PMJDY accounts at 95.92 lakh, followed by Bihar with 62.35 lakh accounts, West Bengal with 37.20 lakh accounts, Assam with 36.30 lakh accounts, and Maharashtra with 36.04 lakh accounts. Inoperative PM Jan Dhan accounts Further, over 15.36 crore (15,36,77,009) accounts were classified as inoperative — that's every fourth account. Among states, again the highest number of inoperative PMJDY accounts were in Uttar Pradesh, which had 3.23 crore such accounts. It was followed by Bihar with 1.59 crore accounts, Madhya Pradesh with 1.35 crore accounts, West Bengal with 1.02 crore accounts, and Maharashtra with 97.94 lakh accounts. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar DM Revamps Leaking School After Spotting Students Studying on Dirt Floor
bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar DM Revamps Leaking School After Spotting Students Studying on Dirt Floor By Anisha Mishra Last Updated: Sep 6, 2026, 13:51 IST District Magistrate Anand Sharma takes swift action to relocate primary students in Madhubani, Bihar, from an unsafe, leaking bamboo hut to a permanent school facility while initiating plans for new, safe infrastructure. Bihar DM Revamps Leaking School After Spotting Students Studying on Dirt Floor Register for Result Updates The District Magistrate of Madhubani, IAS Anand Sharma, took quick action to help primary school students in Bihar. During a surprise inspection in Benipatti block, he saw young children sitting on a dirt floor inside a leaking, makeshift bamboo hut during the rainy season. The administration immediately started a plan to build a better school and moved the students to a safer place. Quick Relocation and Safety Actions Because the temporary bamboo structure was unsafe for students and teachers, the DM stopped classes at the site immediately. Since building a new facility takes several months, he arranged to transfer the students to a nearby permanent school. Moving Students: All primary children were shifted to the nearby Upgraded Middle School Sinuar to continue their classes without any hindrance. Local Directives: The DM, IAS Anand Sharma ordered local education officers to manage the move and provide proper desks and seats for students across schools. Monitoring Progress: Officials received instructions to track daily attendance and make sure the children settled in smoothly. Long-Term Building Plan and Rules To fix the lack of proper school buildings in rural areas, the district administration started a project to construct a new permanent facility for the betterment of students. The DM directed local development teams to speed up the approval process. New School Plan: Officers issued orders to arrange funds and land for a strong school building with clean water and proper toilets requirements Regular Inspections: The DM stated that surprise checks will continue across government schools in Madhubani to maintain basic standards and to avoid any inappropriate activity. Official Accountability: Education officers received warnings that negligence regarding student safety or sub-standard facilities would lead to penalties. By moving the students quickly and planning a permanent campus, the local administration ensured safety and better learning conditions for the children.

bihar_raw_news.title: IIT Madras patents chemical-free antibacterial surface | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 06, 2026 IIT Madras innovation targets antimicrobial resistance Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Source: iitmz The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras has patented a chemical-free antibacterial surface designed to physically destroy harmful bacteria without antibiotics, disinfectants, radiation or antimicrobial chemicals. The technology uses specially engineered nanoscale structures that rupture bacterial cell walls when they come into contact with the surface. Researchers say the approach could offer a new way to tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a growing global health concern in which bacteria become resistant to conventional treatments. Developed by researchers in IIT Madras’ Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, the surface is fabricated on flexible, implant-grade silicone using a customised low-pressure plasma process known as Reactive Ion Etching. The process creates dense arrays of nanoscale “nanograss” structures capable of mechanically damaging bacterial cells. Researchers also identified a stiff surface layer formed during the plasma treatment that helps transfer mechanical forces to bacteria and enhances the bactericidal effect. Tests against three bacterial species showed strong antibacterial activity and more than 68 per cent inhibition of biofilm formation. At the same time, the surfaces remained compatible with mammalian cells, with fibroblast tests recording up to 91 per cent cell viability. The findings, published in ACS Applied Biomaterials, were supported by computational modelling to determine the nanostructure dimensions required to rupture bacterial cells. Researchers said the technology could potentially be used in medical implants, urinary catheters, wound-care products, hospital equipment, pharmaceutical packaging and high-contact public surfaces. The team said its purely mechanical mechanism could reduce concerns over chemical leaching and the development of bacterial resistance. with inputs from PTI 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: TCS Subsidiary HyperVault to Build Rs 70000 Crore AI Data Centre in Hyderabad
bihar_raw_news.content: September 06, 2026 TCS’s HyperVault to build Rs 70,000 Cr AI data centre in Hyderabad Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service HyperVault, a subsidiary of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), on Saturday announced that it has secured 264 acres of land in Hyderabad to develop a large-scale artificial intelligence data centre campus with a total investment outlay of up to Rs 70,000 crore. The purpose-built facility, which will have a capacity of up to 1 Gigawatt (GW), is designed to support frontier AI companies and hyperscalers with high-density, liquid-cooled compute infrastructure on a global scale, the company said in a regulatory filing. “HyperVault, a subsidiary of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), has secured 264 acres of land to develop a large-scale AI data centre campus of up to 1GW capacity in Hyderabad. “The project will generate several thousand direct and indirect jobs in the region. HyperVault and its partners are expected to invest up to Rs 70,000 crore to build and manage this infrastructure,” it said. The project will be executed in a phased manner in line with customer demands and technology requirements. Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy termed the project "historic" for the state and country. "This establishes that Hyderabad is now at the forefront of the global AI revolution with a strong focus on infrastructure. This decade is one of Artificial Intelligence. Access to AI models and compute is fast-becoming public infrastructure, and having this compute reside in Telangana gives us an advantage," he said. The campus will leverage green energy and water-neutral design principles as part of its build-out, the company added. TCS CEO and Managing Director K Krithivasan said the initiative advances the firm's "Infrastructure-to-Intelligence" strategy by integrating AI-ready infrastructure with the company's cloud, AI, and enterprise capabilities. "Hyderabad offers the scale, talent and ecosystem to serve global customers," Krithivasan said. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Shared Peril - The Statesman
bihar_raw_news.content: The catastrophic floods in Nepal should end a dangerous illusion in India: that Himalayan disasters can be neatly contained within national borders or explained simply by blaming an upstream neighbour for “releasing” water. The Himalayan river system does not recognise political boundaries. What happens in Nepal’s mountains can shape the fate of millions in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, just as infrastructure decisions on the Indian side can worsen flooding across Nepal’s Terai. The growing volatility of this shared ecosystem demands a fundamental shift from reactive disaster management to cooperative risk management. India has long treated floods largely as a domestic engineering problem, responding with embankments, barrages, relief camps and compensation. Yet the record suggests that controlling rivers is not the same as understanding them. The 2008 Kosi catastrophe remains an uncomfortable reminder. It was not simply an overwhelming volume of water that devastated Bihar; institutional failure and a breach in an inadequately maintained embankment transformed a manageable river flow into a humanitarian disaster. That distinction matters even more today. Advertisement The Himalayas are producing hazards that increasingly defy the conventional definition of a flood. Cloudbursts, landslides, glacial lake outbursts and rock-and-ice avalanches can unleash torrents carrying enormous quantities of sediment and debris. The 2021 Chamoli disaster and the destruction at Dharali in Uttarakhand last year demonstrated the destructive potential of such events. Nepal’s latest tragedy belongs to the same expanding geography of Himalayan risk. Advertisement Climate change compounds the problem, but invoking it should not become an excuse for institutional fatalism. A warming atmosphere may intensify extreme rainfall, yet human decisions determine much of the eventual damage. Roads and railways obstruct natural drainage; settlements expand across floodplains; embankments deteriorate; hydropower projects proliferate in fragile valleys; and warning systems often fail at the point where they matter most ~ reaching vulnerable communities in time. The India-Nepal relationship consequently needs a more ambitious framework than periodic exchanges of river data. Real-time monitoring must be expanded across vulnerable catchments. Joint forecasting models are needed, along with regular sharing of information on sediment movement, changing river channels, glacial lakes and the structural condition of embankments and barrages. Disaster warnings must also travel beyond government offices to the villages and households directly in harm’s way. This is not merely an environmental issue. North Bihar’s chronic vulnerability affects agriculture, migration, infrastructure and regional economic development. Repeated disasters can trap already poor communities in cycles of asset loss and displacement. The economic consequences of Himalayan instability will increasingly extend far beyond the mountains. The deeper lesson from Nepal is therefore one of interdependence. Neither country can engineer its way to safety independently while sharing rivers whose behaviour is becoming less predictable. The question is no longer whether the next Himalayan disaster will cross a border. It is whether the institutions on both sides will recognise that the border is largely irrelevant to the disaster itself. national_raw_news.content: A multi-storey building collapsed in the Satya Niketan area of New Delhi this afternoon. According to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) New Delhi, four persons were brought to the Trauma Centre for treatment. Of them, one person was brought dead, two persons are in critical condition and one was discharged. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police has said that six persons have been rescued so far and shifted to hospitals. The Police said during the local enquiry it was revealed that the building was 40 to 50 years old and some repair work was underway in the basement of the building when the incident happened. The Delhi Fire Service has deployed 18 fire tenders for the relief and rescue work at the location. Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu has directed all concerned agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, and Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) to work in complete coordination to ensure swift rescue efforts on the ground. In a social media post, Mr Sandhu said that the situation is being closely monitored and it will be ensured that every possible support reaches those in need. He also prayed for the safety and well-being of everyone affected. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta in a social media post said that an adjacent building has also been vacated as a precautionary measure and every possible effort is being made to safely rescue those trapped and provide immediate assistance to affected families. The Chief Minister has directed all concerned agencies to maintain close coordination and ensure a swift response.

national_raw_news.content: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan has urged young people to stay away from drugs and encourage their friends to say no to drugs. Addressing the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Geetanagar College in Guwahati today, he stressed that students must make responsible choices and safeguard their time, health and future. C P Radhakrishnan said India’s young population is its greatest strength and that the opportunities emerging in areas such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, space research and entrepreneurship can enable the youth to play a leading role in building a developed India. Stating that quality education, research, and character building are essential for the nation’s progress he asked educational institutions to go beyond preparing students for careers and focus on creating responsible citizens for democracy and society. The Vice President highlighted the growing achievements of women in higher education, describing it as a welcome transformation and a reflection of Nari Shakti. He noted that providing women with the right education and opportunities enables them to stand on their own feet, which constitutes true empowerment. Referring to Assam’s development trajectory, Radhakrishnan said that over the last five years, Assam’s economy has expanded by 45%, with per capita income rising by 54% from 2021-22 to 2024-25. Emphasizing Prime Minister’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the Vice President said the inclusive development of every state and region, particularly the North East, is essential to achieving this goal. The Vice President is on a two-day visit to Assam starting today. This afternoon, Shri Radhakrishnan will attend the Convocation Ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences at Jyoti-Bishnu Antarjatik Kala Mandir, Guwahati.

national_raw_news.title: IAF Sarang team in Egypt to showcase helicopter precision flying, debut new manoeuvre at ...
national_raw_news.content: IAF Sarang team in Egypt to showcase helicopter precision flying, debut new manoeuvre at El Alamein Airshow Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर IAF Sarang team in Egypt to showcase helicopter precision flying, debut new manoeuvre at El Alamein Airshow ANI | Updated: Sep 06, 2026 17:24 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 6 (ANI): The Indian Air Force’s Sarang Helicopter Display Team are currently present in Egypt to participate in the second edition of the El Alamein International Airshow , scheduled to be held from September 8 to 10 at El Alamein International Airport, according to a statement from the Ministry of Defence issued on Sunday. The Sarang team, the world’s only five-helicopter display team, will showcase its precision, professionalism and flying skills through a series of choreographed aerial displays at the international airshow. The Ministry of Defence said the team’s participation marks another significant milestone in the Indian Air Force’s international engagements and reflects the growing defence and diplomatic ties between India and Egypt . Flying the indigenously designed and manufactured Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Dhruv, the Sarang team is renowned for demanding formation manoeuvres, close-proximity flying and synchronised aerial sequences. During the airshow, the team will perform its famous “Dolphin Leap” manoeuvre and also present a new manoeuvre called the “Spot Stall Turn”. The El Alamein International Airshow brings together leading air forces as well as professionals from the aerospace, defence and space sectors from across the world. The Sarang display over Egypt ian skies will add a distinctive dimension to the event while strengthening ties with international teams participating in the airshow, MoD in its statement added. The Sarang Team was formed in 2002 and flies indigenously built ALH helicopters. The Sarang's first international public display was in Singapore in 2004, and the team was ranked among the top 10 display teams in 2005 at the Al Ain Aerobatic Show in the UAE. Sarang has participated in several prominent international airshows, including the MAKS International Air Show in Russia in 2021, the Dubai Airshow in 2021 and 2023, the Bahrain International Airshow in 2024, and the Singapore Airshow in 2024 and 2026. The team also regularly participates in domestic events and has rendered services during Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief operations. national_raw_news.content: Union Minister Manohar Lal shares video of Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2 inauguration, says Madhya Pradesh is heart of the country Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Minister Manohar Lal shares video of Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2 inauguration, says Madhya Pradesh is heart of the country ANI | Updated: Sep 06, 2026 16:19 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 6 (ANI): Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Manohar Lal, who yesterday inaugurated the Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2, has said that Madhya Pradesh is the heart of the country and Indore is the heartbeat and that if the two are strong, the country will be strong. “Madhya Pradesh is the heart of the country and Indore is the heartbeat of the heart .. If the heart and heartbeat remain strong for the country, then the country will also remain strong,” the Union Minister said in a post on X, posting a video of the inauguration ceremony. The Union Minister inaugurated Metro Priority Corridor–2 on Saturday in the presence of Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav. According to a release from the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, the newly inaugurated phase-I (Reach-II) of approx 11 km, comprising 11-stations, starting from Super Corridor-3 to Malviya Nagar Chauraha, has been developed at an estimated cost of Rs 2,850 crore. With this expansion, the Indore Metro network now comprises 16 operational stations covering approximately 17 km, with a cumulative project cost of about Rs 4,370 crore. In his remarks at the event, Manohar Lal said that the Metro will provide citizens with a faster, safer, more comfortable and reliable mode of transport while strengthening connectivity between residential, commercial and employment centres. The Union Minister emphasised that Metro Rail is not merely a transportation project but an important instrument for economic growth, urban transformation and social inclusion. Increased use of public transport will also help reduce traffic congestion, fuel consumption and emissions. Manohar Lal congratulated the Government of Madhya Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Limited, officials, engineers, workers and all stakeholders associated with the project. In an X post earlier, Lal said Indore's connectivity has gained new momentum through this expansion. "The expansion of the metro network will accelerate the city's industries, trade, and citizen services, while also saving travelers' time, ensuring safe journeys, and helping reduce congestion and traffic pressure in the city. In the upcoming phases, connecting the railway station, airport, and other key locations to the metro network will further boost seamless mobility in Indore. Under the guidance of the respected Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, we are fully committed to enhancing citizens' ‘Ease of Living,’ and the expansion of metro services has emerged as a key part of this endeavor," he said. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 16th National Meet of State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils held at Chandigarh; Deliberations to focus on effective Implementation of the Biodiversity Governance Framework at the State and local levels Governor (Punjab) and Administrator (Chandigarh) highlights importance of combining Traditional Knowledge and Community Participation with Contemporary Approaches of Biodiversity Conservation States, UTs need to align Rules, Institutional Mechanisms and Implementation Processes with amended National Biodiversity Governance Framework: Union Environment Minister Dynamic Local Level Planning imperative for documenting Local Biodiversity and Traditional Knowledge that contribute to Sustainable Development: Shri Bhupender Yadav Posted On: 06 SEP 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi Chandigarh/New Delhi, 6th September, 2026 The 16th National Meet of the State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) was inaugurated today at Chandigarh. Organised by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), the two-day National Meet, being held from 6–7 September 2026, brings together Chairpersons and Member Secretaries of SBBs and UTBCs from across the country, along with senior officials, experts and scientists. The inaugural session was presided over by Governor of Punjab and Administrator, UT Chandigarh, Shri Gulab Chand Kataria; Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav; and Minister for Environment, Forest and Wildlife, Government of Haryana, Shri Rao Narbir Singh. Other dignitaries present in the occasion included Secretary, MoEFCC, Shri Tanmay Kumar; Director General of Forests and Special Secretary, MoEFCC, Shri Sushil Kumar Awasthi; Additional Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Ashutosh Agnihotri; Chairperson, National Biodiversity Airport (NBA), Shri Virendra Tiwari; and other senior officials of the Union Ministry, besides those from SBBs and UTBCs. Addressing the gathering, Shri Gulab Chand Kataria highlighted India’s rich biological heritage and traditional environmental ethos. He emphasised that ecological security is closely linked with food and water security, livelihoods and sustainable development, and underlined the importance of combining traditional knowledge and community participation with contemporary approaches. The Governor drew attention to the ecological significance of its wetlands, riverine ecosystems and agricultural biodiversity. He stressed the importance of strengthening Biodiversity Management Committees and People’s Biodiversity Registers and called for stronger coordination among biodiversity institutions and local communities. In his address on the occasion, Shri Bhupender Yadav highlighted India’s long-standing environmental ethos and referred to initiatives under the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi like Mission LiFE, Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam, Amrit Sarovar and the Green Credit Programme. India takes along its scientific prowess as well as traditional community wisdom together in this conservation journey, he stated. Referring to the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, the Minister noted that the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 and the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024 have further strengthened and streamlined the biodiversity governance framework. He urged States and Union Territories to align their rules, institutional mechanisms and implementation processes with the amended framework. The Minister appreciated India’s progress in fulfilling its international biodiversity commitments, including the submission of the 7th National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity and the 1st National Report on the Nagoya Protocol...

national_raw_news.content: Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2 Inaugurated, Network Expands To 16 Operational Stations Covering Around 17 Km Infrastructure Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2 Inaugurated, Network Expands To 16 Operational Stations Covering Around 17 Km Swarajya Staff Sep 06, 2026 | Updated 09:24 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Indore Metro priority corridor-2 has been inaugurated (Pic Via PIB) Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav yesterday (5 September) inaugurated the Indore Metro Priority corridor-2 at the Brilliant Convention Centre in Vijay Nagar. Regular passenger services on the expanded Gandhi Nagar-Malviya Nagar Square corridor began today, marking a significant milestone for Madhya Pradesh's commercial capital. The operational network has expanded from approximately 6 km to 17 km, with the extended corridor covering 16 stations. The first train departs at 9 am, while the last train operates at 7 pm, with Metro trains available every 15 minutes and more than 80 trips scheduled daily. The initial 6 km priority section entered operations on 31st May 2025 and was officially inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi via video conferencing from Bhopal. The new 11 km extension runs from Super Corridor-3 to Malviya Nagar Chauraha, also known as Radisson Square, bringing Metro services closer to key residential and commercial areas across the city. The newly inaugurated phase-I (Reach-II) of approx 11 km comprising 11-stations starting from Super Corridor-3 to Malviya Nagar Chauraha and has been developed at an estimated cost of Rs 2,850 crore. With this expansion, the Indore Metro network now comprises 16 operational stations covering approximately 17 km, with a cumulative project cost of about Rs 4,370 crore. The Asian Development Bank had last year approved a $190 million loan to support development of an 8.62 kilometre underground metro line with seven stations, connecting congested areas to the airport. Chief Minister Yadav said the second phase marked the metro's gradual movement from the outskirts towards more populated parts of Indore, with the planned Yellow Line eventually continuing beyond Malviya Nagar towards Shaheed Bagicha, Khajrana Chauraha, Bengali Chauraha, Patrakar Colony and Palasia before reaching the railway station. The corridor received approval from the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety in March 2026.
